stories.title: Madagascar ex-Senate chief sentenced to hard labour over deadly Gen Z protest crackdown
stories.summary: Madagascar's former Senate president has been sentenced to 10 years of hard labour over his alleged role in the violent crackdown on youth-led protests that helped bring down the previous government last year. Richard Ravalomanana, a retired general and close ally of former President Andry Rajoelina, was found guilty of complicity in murder by a court in the capital, Antananarivo, on Tuesday. Prosecutors accused him of giving instructions to security forces to use violence against demonstrators during the so-called Gen Z protests in September and October 2025. Ravalomanana denied the allegations and said he would appeal against the judgement. From prison to presidential palace: Who is Madagascar's new military ruler? The protests began a year ago, initially sparked by anger over persistent power and water shortages, before developing into a broader movement against Rajoelina's government. At least 22 people were killed and more than 100 injured during the unrest, according to UN figures cited by local media. The protests eventually triggered a political crisis that led to Rajoelina's removal from power and the installation of a new administration led by Col Michael Randrianirina. The crackdown was led by the gendarmerie, where Ravalomanana retained considerable influence at the time. He "directed violent actions to suppress the demonstrations", a state prosecutor said in December 2025. Ravalomanana was removed as Senate president in October, shortly after the protests, and was arrested at his home in December after failing to respond to a summons from the gendarmerie. He was later placed in pre-trial detention at the high-security Imerintsiatosika prison outside Antananarivo, where he has spent the past seven months.

stories.headline: Man arrested as Hong Kong customs seizes HK$42 million worth of ‘space oil’

opening: Hong Kong customs has arrested a man and seized HK$42 million (US$5.3 million) worth of the illegal narcotic “space oil” from a drug workshop fitted with a semi-automated production line capable of producing up to 160,000 cartridges in a short period.

Senior investigator Chan Kit-lun of the Customs and Excise Department’s drug investigation bureau said officers intercepted a suspicious man on Tuesday and escorted him to a property in Kam Tin, Yuen Long.

stories.headline: Saleswoman arrested over aggressive sales tactics, third suspect linked to Opatra

opening: Hong Kong customs officers have arrested a woman for allegedly using aggressive tactics to sell skincare products at a local beauty chain formerly operating under the Opatra London brand, bringing the number of arrests in the case to three, the South China Morning Post has learned.

A source said the saleswoman, who is in her twenties, was suspected of pressuring a customer into making purchases at the now-closed Sha Tin New Town Plaza outlet, which was formerly operated by Sayles Retail.
